perf.summary: Replace the full QuickSort after each prime with an in-place 2-way merge; the appended block is already sorted ascending and so is the existing prefix.
perf.currentCost: For each of the b primes, QuickSort(result,0,count-1) re-sorts the entire current array: O(b * count * log count) comparisons/swaps overall, with deep recursion and poor cache behavior. count grows up to the final smooth-number count (can be thousands).
perf.proposedChange: Each prime's inner loop appends, for every existing entry result[j], the chain result[j]*p, result[j]*p^2, ... in ascending order into result[count..]. The pre-existing [0,curCount) region is already sorted from the previous pass. So instead of QuickSort, do a single linear merge of the two sorted runs [0,curCount) and [curCount,count) into a scratch (or merge from the back in place) in O(count) time. This removes the sort entirely.
perf.rationale: Turns O(b * n log n) total work into O(b * n) with sequential memory access that Burst/HW-prefetch handle far better, and eliminates recursive QuickSort call overhead and its O(log n) stack frames.
perf.risk: Must confirm the appended run is globally monotonic. Within one j the chain val*p < val*p^2 is ascending, but across different j the runs interleave, so the appended region [curCount,count) is NOT itself fully sorted unless generated by interleaving. Safer formulation: generate the appended values then merge per-j, or collect appended values and merge once. If a clean 2-run split is not guaranteed, fall back to bottom-up merge of the naturally-sorted sub-runs. No numeric/overflow change (val<=limit/p guards overflow as before).

perf.summary: If the sort must stay, make it iterative/median-of-three with an insertion-sort cutoff to avoid deep recursion and worst-case stacks under Burst.
perf.currentCost: Recursive QuickSort with median-of-three-by-position pivot; recursion depth and per-call overhead are not ideal under Burst, which does not optimize recursion well, and worst-case inputs give O(n^2) and O(n) recursion depth.
perf.proposedChange: Convert to an explicit stackalloc index-stack loop, recurse into the smaller partition first (bounded O(log n) stack), and switch to insertion sort for sub-arrays under ~16 elements.
perf.rationale: Removes call overhead Burst cannot inline through recursion, bounds stack to O(log n), and insertion-sort cutoff cuts constant factors on the many tiny partitions.
perf.risk: Pure refactor of an internal helper; identical ordering output. Only relevant if the merge replacement above is not adopted.
